citation: 'The Great fire at Chicago. Scene in Wells Street - the terrified populace in front of the Briggs House.' Wood engraving, Frank Leslie's Illustrated Newspaper, 28 October 1871. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LC-USZ62-109590 (item 94501371).
author: Frank Leslie's Illustrated Newspaper
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division; reproduction 3c09590v.jpg at tile.loc.gov. The catalogue note names Harper's Weekly; the masthead on the page is Frank Leslie's.
locator: The whole cut: the street crowd in the foreground, a steam fire engine at the left.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' A reference picture only; nothing traced or sampled.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-19 (T-3690). An artist's engraving made within three weeks of the fire, not a photograph: the men in felt hats, round and soft, and sack coats, many bearded; the women in day dresses to the ground with shawls and small hats; people carrying bundles and trunks; a horse-drawn steam fire engine.
what_it_supplies: what an engraver of 1871 drew Chicago's street crowd wearing: felt hats, sack coats, beards and side whiskers; women's long skirts, shawls and small hats
what_it_does_not_supply: a photograph's exactness; any named person; colour
note: The street crowd the 1871 town wardrobe is checked against (L-wardrobe-1871).
